newsitem.title: UK: London gold firmer, but seen range bound for now.
newsitem.headline: London gold firmer, but seen range bound for now.

text.p: Gold prices spurted higher on short covering on Tuesday in early Europe after recent gains eroded somewhat during Asian trading hours.
But prices remained wedged in the $350-$355 trading range of the past three days.
Bullion fixed at $353.45 an ounce, up slightly from Monday's afternoon's fixing of $353.05 and about $1.75 higher than the lows in Asia.
"Gold was sold down overnight and people were caught short this morning, so we saw a bit of scramble," a dealer said.
Australian producer selling had helped depress prices during Asian trading, he added.
Technical analysts said gold may move sideways for the time being, but looked to extend the gains it has made since recovering from 3-3/4 year lows of $336 an ounce earlier this month.
"It is slightly overbought, and I emphasise slightly, so we may see some consolidation before a challenge of $360.30," said Karen Jones of Credit Suisse.
The market was also seen hanging back from any sizable moves ahead of testimony this week from U.S. Federal Reserve chairman Alan Greenspan.
Dealers will be watching Greenspan's Wednesday report to Congress on the state of the economy for hints on the course of inflation and changes in U.S. interest rates.
But the market took heart from comments on Monday from the Belgian central bank chairman Alfons Verplaetse that the Belgian central bank had a good balance of gold in its reserves after recent sales.
Like gold, platinum was solid at $373.50/$374.50, up $0.50 from Monday's London close. Technically platinum was targetting $374 and then $380, analysts said.
Palladium was even firmer at $139.25/$140.25, up $1.50.
Both metals were exhibiting a positive tone amid continued delays in palladium supply contracts between Russian producers and Japanese consumers, dealers said.
Backgrounding the delayed contracts was potential labour problems in Russia's cash-strapped Norilsk Nickel plant, which produces platinum group metals.
Silver, in contrast to the others, was lacklustre, indicated one cent weaker at $5.20/$5.21.
"There has been some unwinding of the plays on the gold-silver ratio, with people now buying gold and selling silver," a dealer said.
